subject: Action required: your password expires in 2 hours
body:
Dear user,

Our records show your password will expire in the next 2 hours. To avoid losing access to email and files, verify your account immediately using the secure link below.

[ Verify my account now ]

IT Helpdesk
flags: The domain is a lookalike: rnicrosoft, not microsoft.
Urgency and a countdown are used to rush you.
A generic "Dear user" greeting, not your name.
It asks you to "verify" by following a link.

subject: Reminder: timesheets due this Friday
body:
Hi team,

Just a reminder that timesheets are due by 5pm Friday. If you have any leave to record, please add it before then.

Thanks,
Jane
flags: The sender is a known colleague on your real company domain.
It is a routine, expected message with no links or attachments.
There is no urgency, threat, or request for credentials or money.
Still worth a quick sanity check, but this one looks genuine.

subject: Quick favour - are you at your desk?
body:
Hi,

I'm about to go into a meeting and need you to sort something for me urgently. Can you purchase four $100 gift cards for a client and send me the codes? I'll reimburse you today. Keep this between us for now.

Mark
flags: The "CEO" is emailing from a personal Gmail, not the company domain.
A gift card request is a classic scam pattern.
Urgency plus secrecy ("keep this between us").
An unusual request that bypasses normal process.

subject: Your parcel is on hold - $3.50 fee required
body:
Your parcel could not be delivered because a small customs fee of $3.50 is outstanding. Pay now to release your parcel, or it will be returned to sender within 24 hours.

[ Pay $3.50 and release parcel ]
flags: The domain auspost-parcel.net is not the real Australia Post domain.
A tiny fee is used to harvest your card details.
Pressure with a 24-hour deadline.
You were not expecting a fee for a delivery.

subject: Unusual sign-in detected - verify it was you
body:
We detected a sign-in to your account from a new device in another country. If this was not you, secure your account now.

[ Review activity ]

Microsoft account team
flags: The domain microsoftonline-support.com is not a genuine Microsoft domain.
Fear (a foreign sign-in) is used to make you click fast.
The button leads to a fake login page to steal your password.
Real alerts are best checked by going to the service directly, not via the email link.

subject: Invoice INV-2043 from your supplier is ready
body:
An invoice has been shared with you in Xero. You can log in to your Xero account to review and pay it.

Log in at xero.com as you normally would.
flags: The domain post.xero.com is a genuine Xero sending address.
It does not ask for your password inside the email.
It suggests logging in the normal way, not via a suspicious link.
If you use Xero and expected an invoice, this is likely genuine. Still, log in directly rather than clicking through.

subject: Update your bank details for this pay run
body:
Hi,

We are updating our payroll system. Please reply with your bank account and BSB so we can make sure your pay lands correctly this cycle.

Payroll Team
flags: The domain is yourcompany.co, a lookalike of the real yourcompany.com.au.
It asks for bank details by email, which payroll would never do.
Changing where pay is deposited is a common fraud goal.
Verify any bank-detail change in person or by a known phone number.
